chunks: And from him, from Abbas, from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) kills the black snake (Aswad al-Ghadar), the viper, the scorpion, and the mouse, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named them the 'Fasiqah' (the wicked one) and 'al-Fuwaysiqah' (the little wicked one). He throws the raven, and he said: 'Kill everything from them that wants you.'

key_terms.الْأَسْوَدَ الْغَدِرَ: The black snake (specifically the Aswad snake)
key_terms.الْفَاسِقَةَ: The wicked one (a name given to certain creatures)
key_terms.الْفُوَيْسِقَةَ: The little wicked one (diminutive form of Fasiqah)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What creatures can a pilgrim in Ihram kill according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fauna—black snake, viper, scorpion, and mouse—that a Muhrim may kill without incurring penalty, distinguishing them by the Prophet’s designation of 'al-Fasiqah' and 'al-Fuwaysiqah' to signify their transgression against the sanctity of the Haram. It establishes a practical legal principle where the threat to the pilgrim justifies the removal of these creatures, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity with physical safety during Hajj and Umrah.
